verdicts.quote: the product ships a Lightning app and a tab (names in AD-4) that show the chat component full-width. A user holding the product's permission set sees the app in App Launcher and can open the tab by URL
(c) The controller reads and writes no Salesforce record data and does not pass any org data to xAI beyond what the user typed; the bot has no action it can take in the org.
Object CRUD/FLS: not applicable because no standard or custom object is read or written; the Custom Metadata read is of the app's own configuration type.
`Grok_Bot_User` grants: visibility of tab `Grok_Bot` and app `Grok_Bot_App`; access to `GrokBotController` ... External Credential principal access
verdicts.missing: Use is gated by a permission set, but administration is only 'admins in Setup' / 'Setup users with credential admin rights'; no named permission or permission set defines who may administer the bot.

verdicts.quote: That browser session only; sent to xAI per send (R-9); not readable by other Salesforce users or admins
one callout per transaction (platform limit 100), no DML so the "callout after pending DML" restriction cannot trigger.
verdicts.missing: The spec deals with the DML-before-callout restriction but rejects an asynchronous design and runs the callout synchronously (AD-1). It never addresses the trigger constraint and adopts no Queueable/future/batch design.

verdicts.quote: API key stored only as an External Credential secret (R-11 A3 proves none in source; Setup shows the parameter masked)
100 callouts/transaction, 120 s cumulative timeout, 10 s default, 120 000 ms maximum per callout, no callout after pending DML
verdicts.missing: Heap is explicitly 'not verified here and is not asserted', and CPU time is not mentioned; no numbers are given for either.

verdicts.quote: Apex: `GrokBotControllerTest`/`GrokClientTest` with `HttpCalloutMock` ... none uses the real xAI endpoint
Named Credential | `Grok_API` (URL `https://api.x.ai/v1`, bound to `Grok_xAI`)
browser LWC `grokBot` → imperative Apex call `GrokBotController.send` ... Rejected: ... Apex Queueable/async
verdicts.missing: The UI learns of the reply only because the synchronous Apex call returns inline. No event, CDC, polled status or LMS mechanism is defined.

verdicts.quote: Duplicates / ordering: single in-flight guard (T-9); no idempotency key because no retry is automatic.
One in-flight send per component; Send disabled while pending (R-2 A5); two tabs have independent transcripts
verdicts.missing: No org-wide concurrency limit (e.g. concurrent long-running Apex requests) is named, and nothing says what happens to a request rejected for capacity.

verdicts.quote: xAI HTTP 5xx | UPSTREAM | "Grok is temporarily unavailable. Try again." | `CalloutException` read timeout | TIMEOUT ... Any other HTTP 4xx ... | REQUEST
No automatic retry (a retry could bill twice and cannot be proven safe). ... xAI HTTP 429 | RATE_LIMIT | "Grok is rate-limiting requests. Try again shortly."
The reply length is capped by *K* = 1024 tokens ... `CalloutException` read timeout | TIMEOUT | "Grok took too long to answer. Try again."
verdicts.missing: The never-arrives case is covered by TIMEOUT, but a reply truncated at the token cap (finish_reason 'length') has no stated detection or user-visible indication.

verdicts.quote: The product stores no transcript anywhere (see State table), logs no message text (R-10), and keeps no xAI response id.
verdicts.missing: The spec deliberately stores no conversation records, so there is no record shape with role, status, timestamps, model identifier or token/usage counts, and usage is not captured anywhere.

verdicts.quote: New chat (R-13, F-2), page reload, navigation away: all clear it. No persistence
does not pass any org data to xAI beyond what the user typed ... "Messages are sent to xAI. Don't enter confidential or customer data."
Only the most recent *N* = 20 messages (default; configurable per R-8) ending with the new user message are transmitted; earlier ones stay visible in the UI but are not sent.

before the first message the transcript area shows "Ask Grok anything." ... a message that is empty after trim is not sent ... a 4000-character message is accepted; a 4001-character message is refused
Changing a value in Setup (Custom Metadata) takes effect on the next send with no redeploy. ... logged at INFO with outcome code (`OK` or an errorCode)
verdicts.missing: Changing the model is covered, and failures are visible only through debug logs. There is no explicit way to turn the bot off (no enable flag or kill switch).

verdicts.quote: each send produces one correlation id ... logged at INFO with outcome code ... No log line contains the message text, reply text
verdicts.missing: No audit record of who asked what and what was answered. The log omits content and identity, and its retention is left to platform policy.

verdicts.quote: deploys to the target development org with a single `sf project deploy start --target-org <alias>` ... Org-level coverage gate for a non-dev target: unresolved, not applicable to a development org.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credential differ per environment (dev vs sandbox vs production) and the production 75% coverage requirement are not decided.

verdicts.quote: pending state appears synchronously on send (A2 of R-2), a hard cap of *T* (60 s default, ≤120 s platform cumulative limit, AD-1)
Designed states: empty (R-2 A1), pending (indicator, Send disabled), error (R-6 text + Retry), config-missing (R-6 CONFIG text); none shows raw JSON or a blank card.
deploys additively (no deletion or overwrite of existing org metadata) ... Anything already in the org stays untouched.
